# pro-football-reference.com API

Access NFL statistics, schedules, standings, game boxscores, play-by-play data, and player profiles from Pro-Football-Reference.com

## Install / import

```python
from parse_apis.pro_football_reference_com_api import ProFootballReference
```

## Operations

Call these on the client's collection accessors (e.g. `client.<collection>.<op>(…)`) or via active-record navigation on returned objects — see [`example.py`](./example.py) for the exact call spelling. List operations return a lazy `Paginator`.

| Call | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `game.details(table_id: GameTable \| Literal['pbp', 'vis_drives', 'drive_chart', 'home_drives'])` | `GameDetail` | Retrieve specific detailed tables for an NFL game such as play-by-play or drive charts. Returns row-level data whose fields vary by table type. Play-by-play includes quarter, down, distance, detail text, and expected points. Drive tables include drive number, start position, plays, yards, and result. |
| `game.boxscore()` | `Boxscore` | Retrieve detailed boxscore data for a specific NFL game. Returns team scores, game metadata (roof, surface, duration, attendance, Vegas line), and player-level offensive and defensive statistics. The game_id is available from get_season_schedule results. |
| `client.games.get(game_id: str)` | `Game` | Retrieve detailed boxscore data for a specific NFL game. Returns team scores, game metadata (roof, surface, duration, attendance, Vegas line), and player-level offensive and defensive statistics. The game_id is available from get_season_schedule results. |
| `client.players.search(query: str, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Player]` | Search for NFL players by name to find their player IDs and profile URLs. If the search matches a single player exactly, PFR redirects to that player's page directly and the result contains one entry. Otherwise returns a list of matching players. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `player.profile()` | `PlayerProfile` | Retrieve a player's biographical profile and career stats summary. Returns name, position, college, birthdate, and career statistics tables (passing, rushing, receiving, and/or defense depending on position). The player_id is available from search_players results. |
| `client.players.get(player_id: str)` | `Player` | Retrieve a player's biographical profile and career stats summary. Returns name, position, college, birthdate, and career statistics tables (passing, rushing, receiving, and/or defense depending on position). The player_id is available from search_players results. |
| `season.stats(category: StatCategory \| Literal['defense', 'kicking', 'passing', 'returns', 'rushing', 'scoring', 'receiving'])` | `StatLeaders` | Retrieve statistical leaders for a given NFL season and category. Returns all qualifying players ranked by the primary stat for that category (e.g. pass_yds for passing, rush_yds for rushing). Fields in each player object vary by category. |
| `season.schedule()` | `Schedule` | Retrieve the full NFL schedule for a given season. Returns every regular-season and playoff game with final scores, yardage totals, turnover counts, and a game_id suitable for drill-down into boxscores and play-by-play. One request per season; no pagination. |
| `season.standings()` | `Standings` | Retrieve conference standings for a given NFL season. Returns teams grouped by AFC and NFC with wins, losses, points scored/allowed, margin of victory, and strength of schedule metrics. |
| `client.game(game_id: str)` | `Game` | Constructs a local `Game` handle from a known `game_id` — no request is made. |
| `client.player(player_id: str)` | `Player` | Constructs a local `Player` handle from a known `player_id` — no request is made. |
| `client.season(year: str)` | `Season` | Constructs a local `Season` handle from a known `year` — no request is made. |

## Errors

| Error | Raised when | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `PlayerNotFound` | Player ID does not match any player page (404 from upstream) | `player_id` |
| `InvalidCategory` | Stat category is not one of the accepted values | `category` |

Runtime errors (`RateLimitError`, `UpstreamError`, `PaginationLimitError`, …) are importable from `parse_apis` and can occur on any call.

> **Note.** Some params accept an enum whose corresponding output field is raw `str`/`list` (the wire value isn't bound to the enum). Enum members never compare equal to raw strings — compare such output values against `member.value`, or use plain string literals.
